newsitem.title: USA: U.S. October light vehicle sales rise 2.2 percent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. October light vehicle sales rise 2.2 percent.

text.p: U.S. car and light truck sales during the month of October totaled 1,270,216 units with all automakers reporting, a 2.2 percent increase from the 1,196,262 units sold a year earlier.

The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for the month was 14.93 million units, up from 14.22 million units a year earlier, and down from 15.02 million units for the month of September. The rate is calculated with seasonal factors supplied by the U.S. Commerce Department.
Automakers sold 565,361 North American-built cars in the United States in October, down 7.3 percent from a year ago on a daily selling basis. October had 27 selling days, compared to 26 a year ago.
The seasonally adjusted annual rate for domestic cars was 6.54 million units, compared with 7.17 million in September and 6.91 million in October 1995.

Automakers sold 554,889 domestic trucks in the United States during October, up 15.3 percent from a year earlier. The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for domestic trucks was 6.60 million units, compared with 5.50 million a year earlier and 6.01 million in September.

Imported car sales totaled 112,721 units, down 4.9 percent from a year ago, with a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.36 million units. Imported truck sales rose 15.1 percent to 37,245 units for an annual rate of 440,000 units.
